 Frost Advisory is in effect Deputies: How drones, K-9s caught teens after stolen car crashed into Simpsonville home 
 After crashing, both the driver and the passenger ran from the scene, according to deputies. By Lorenza Medley Published : Oct. 25, 2026 at 1:09 PM EDT | Updated : 16 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google SIMPSONVILLE, S.C. (FOX Carolina) - The Greenville County Sheriff’s Office said drones and multiple K-9 units were used to capture two teen suspects who crashed a stolen car into a Simpsonville home earlier this month .
 Deputies said they tried to make a traffic stop on a stolen vehicle on Oct. 15 when the driver fled.
 The driver then crashed into a home on Renwood Road. After crashing, both the driver and the passenger ran from the scene, according to deputies.
 “When someone decides to run from law enforcement in Greenville County, they quickly learn that our deputies have more than one way to find them,” deputies said.
 In a Facebook post on Saturday, deputies said K-9 teams deployed multiple dogs to trace the path of the driver. Drones were also used to provide an aerial view of the area and another set of eyes from above.
 While tracking the driver, deputies chased down and arrested the passenger on foot.
 According to deputies, two K-9 units searched for the driver in a nearby swampy area, where one of the dogs discovered the driver’s pants and footprints.
 Deputies said the driver crossed into Spartanburg County, where he was quickly taken into custody.
 A 16-year-old and a 15-year-old have both been charged with possession of a stolen vehicle.
 “You can run, but our deputies have a pretty impressive toolbox. And they know how to use it,” deputies said.
 No injuries were reported in the incident, according to officials.
